phone_ban.why: X stays plausible: smuggling fades as quota and sub-threshold models arrive. Y shows workarounds driving FX pressure to 100, but legal supply reaching 100 under a ban is absurd, and assemblers repeat one action.

free_coder.why: Y shows a downturn turning rate cuts into layoffs and emigration, a real turning point for outsourcers. X has employment and hours rising while in-house AI hits 80, a generic and implausibly rosy story.

water_ration.why: Y exposes the trade-off that free tankers drain the utility budget, so repairs stop and rationing tightens. Its tanker vendors are oddly passive, but it is more decision-relevant than X's rain-assisted easing.

truck_strike.why: X has a believable arc: concessions (fuel cut, tariff floor) lead to a deal and recovery. Y repeats escorts and union holding, and prices climb to 93 with little explanation, so the path reads mechanical.
